intro: The analysis is designed to make every assumption explicit and testable. Table 20 lists the methodological risks a framework of this kind faces and how each is treated: removed by the method, or bounded — measured, bounded and disclosed, with the reason it cannot be removed today and the step that resolves it. No risk is left without either a removal or a named resolution.

rows.risk: Policy endogeneity biases the Phillips slope
rows.treatment: IV with lagged gap and world gap (F = 500); two-way fixed effects; slope 0.12–0.19 across estimators. The instruments are not provably exogenous to global supply shocks, so sensitivity extends to 0.25
rows.resolution: Re-estimated with every annual release; κ up to 0.25 already in the stress tests

rows.risk: Output gaps and scenarios use later data
rows.treatment: Real-time test on IMF vintages; the 2021 scenario uses only what was published by 31 December 2021. Financial accounts are revised and their latest release is used
rows.resolution: From now on every release is archived with its vintage, so first releases become available

inherent: Beyond the register, five uncertainties are inherent: future energy prices, the largest source of forecast error; turning points, where every statistical early warning understates risk; the persistence of core inflation after large shocks, which a linear Phillips curve understates (§7.2); the behavioural parameters, until the trials report; and omitted channels — the model has no banking sector, exchange-rate channel beyond energy and oil prices in euro, or fiscal reaction to the premium. The institutional route requires an intergovernmental agreement, national legislation and, for the Digital Euro route, the Digital Euro regulation.
